deep.reconstruction:
The main body of this folio is not Gauss's handwriting. It is p. 50 of a printed German elementary arithmetic textbook (Dritter Abschnitt, 'Von den Proportionen'). The only Gauss material is the cut-off column of handwritten notes on the facing leaf at the right edge. The full version of those notes is on the next page.

PRINTED TEXT

§124 (theorem begun on p. 49). In an arithmetic proportion a-b = c-d, the sum of the extremes equals the sum of the means. In a geometric proportion a:b = c:d, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means.
Proof via §123: write the general arithmetic proportion as a-(a+d) = p-(p+d) and the geometric one as a:(ae) = p:(pe).
(1) Extremes a+(p+d) and means (a+d)+p are equal by commutativity of addition.
(2) Extremes a·pe and means ae·p are equal by commutativity of multiplication.

§125 (converse). Two pairs with equal sum or equal product can always be put into a proportion.
- If a+g = b+c then a-b = c-g.
- If ad = bc then a:b = c:d (tacitly b, d nonzero).

§126. One may choose which pair is extremes and which is means, and the order within each pair. So every proportion admits 8 arrangements; these are the symmetries of the relation x1+x4 = x2+x3 (resp. x1·x4 = x2·x3).
- Arithmetic: a-b=c-g, b-a=g-c, g-b=c-a, c-a=g-b, a-c=b-g, b-g=a-c, g-c=b-a, c-g=a-b.
- Geometric: a:b=c:d, b:a=d:c, d:b=c:a, c:a=d:b, a:c=b:d, b:d=a:c, d:c=b:a, c:d=a:b.

§127 (statement only; the proof is on the next page). The fourth term is b+c-a (arithmetic) or bc/a (geometric). This follows at once from §124.

GAUSS'S MARGINAL NOTES (facing leaf, fragmentary)

The fully legible version is on the next page.

1. Convergents of sqrt(17) = [4; 8, 8, 8, ...]: 4/1, 33/8, 268/65, ..., 9478657/2298912. They obey p_{n+1} = 8p_n + p_{n-1}, and the next page gives the decimal 4.1231056256... = sqrt(17).

2. Tests on the numerator 9478657, written as square ± small numbers (2×..., 3×...). Among them:
   - 9478657 = 2·2177² - 1, the Pell duplication formula x_{2n+1} = 2x_n² - 1, since 2177² - 17·528² = 1;
   - the factorization 9478657 = 79·119983.

3. A scheme for the continued-fraction / reduction algorithm for sqrt(μ):
   - remainders aa-μ, bb-μ, cc-μ;
   - products PR = xx' - μyy', PS = x'x'' - μy'y'', PT = x''x''' - μy''y''';
   - numerators x' = aq - P, x'' = aqr - rP - a, rewritten as the recurrence x'' = rx' - x, y'' = ry' - y.
   On this page only the left edges of these lines are visible ('x'=aq', 'x''=aqr', 'x''=rx'').

This is the standard machinery of the Pell equation and the reduction of the form x² - μy², treated by Gauss in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §§183-205.
errors: The printed text has no mathematical errors. All 8 arithmetic and 8 geometric permutations in §126 are valid consequences of a+g=b+c and ad=bc respectively.
§125 (ad=bc implies a:b=c:d) tacitly assumes b and d are nonzero. This is standard for an elementary text and not a real error.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine printed elementary textbook page on proportions. The only Gauss content is a fragmentary marginal computation of sqrt(17) convergents and Pell-equation numerics, squarely within his well-known published work on continued fractions and quadratic forms.

checkable.asserts: 9478657/2298912 gives a solution of the Pell equation x^2-17y^2=1
2177/528 is a Pell solution for D=17
33/8 is the fundamental Pell solution for D=17
§124 arithmetic case: extremes sum minus means sum equals 0
§124 geometric case: product of extremes equals product of means
§127: fourth term bc/a satisfies the product rule

transcription_corrections: Clarify: the page body is a printed textbook page, not Gauss manuscript. Only the right-edge facing-leaf fragments are Gauss's hand.
Facing-leaf fragment 'PT = x[?]' is the start of 'PT = x''x''' - μy''y''''.
Facing-leaf 'x' = aq[?]' is 'x' = aq - P; y' = q'. 'x'' = aqr[?]' is 'x'' = aqr - rP - a'.
Facing-leaf 'x'' = rx'[?]' is 'x'' = rx' - x, y'' = ry' - y' (an earlier cancelled variant x'' = x' - a appears on the next page).
The '1 2' and '4/1 33/8' at the top are the start of the indexed convergent list 1...9 of sqrt(17).
